steps.do: List every nav widget class used in the app so the plan has a complete source list.

Write docs/a11y/nav_plan.md with one row per destination holding its index, label, icon, and tooltip.
Mark any row whose label is empty or is only an icon asset name as a gap to fix.
List the nav directory so the plan cites real file paths.
Run the label test in test/a11y/nav_labels_test.dart. It must print 'All tests passed!' and cover every destination in the plan.

Using an icon asset name as the accessible label instead of a user-facing word.

K-023640.check: rg lists each color literal, and the ratio column in nav_plan.md has a value of at least 4.5 for every text row and at least 3.0 for every icon row.

Using the 3:1 threshold for body text, which needs 4.5:1.
Estimating ratios by eye instead of computing the luminance formula.

steps.do: Create the test file that will wrap SignupForm in a Profiler with id SignupForm and an onRender callback that pushes each commit into an array.
Install the test runner, testing library, user-event helper, and jsdom if they are missing.

K-023644.check: vitest prints Tests 1 passed, and the assertion expect(commits.length).toBe(10) holds.

steps.do: Create the Playwright spec file for input latency.
Install the Playwright test package as a dev dependency.
Download the Chromium browser that Playwright uses for the test.

In the spec, go to /signup, focus the email field, and for each of 20 keys record performance.now before the press and after the next requestAnimationFrame, then compute the p95 of the deltas and log it.
Run the spec and read the logged p95 value.

K-023645.example: The spec types 20 characters and logs a p95 delta of 46ms, which passes the 200ms budget. If p95 is above 200ms, move the error and validation update into startTransition or wrap the derived value in useDeferredValue.
K-023645.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and the logged line shows p95 keystroke latency below 200ms.
traps: Do not use fill(), because it sets the whole value in one event and hides the per-key cost; use pressSequentially instead.
Do not raise the 200ms budget to make a failing run pass.
Do not run only against the Vite dev server and report the number as production performance.

Read the total blocking time in milliseconds from the report.
Confirm the printed value is below 200 milliseconds, and repeat the Lighthouse run two more times to check it is stable.

K-023646.example: The report prints 143.6 for total-blocking-time, under the 200ms budget. If it prints a value above 200, check whether a heavy validation library such as zod is imported eagerly into the signup route chunk.
K-023646.check: jq prints a number such as 143.6, and that number is less than 200.
traps: Do not run Lighthouse against the dev server, because unminified dev code inflates blocking time.
Do not trust a single run, since the value varies between runs.
Do not report the performance score alone when the total blocking time value is the number to check.

steps.do: Print the name of English as written in German, to confirm the browser runtime supports the API.
Print the name of German as written in English, to confirm the reverse lookup works.
Plan to build each option label from Intl.DisplayNames with the current locale, so no language names are stored in message files.

K-023650.example: The first command prints Englisch and the second prints German. The select builds labels from new Intl.DisplayNames($locale, { type: 'language' }) at render time.
K-023650.check: The first command prints Englisch and the second prints German. If either prints the code instead of a name, the runtime lacks the data.

Intl.DisplayNames needs a locale argument. Passing undefined or an empty string can throw a RangeError.

steps.do: Check whether the select stylesheet already sets a minimum height.
Check the root font size, which sets what 1rem resolves to.
Plan a minimum height of 44px, which is 2.75rem at a 16px root size, on the select and its option list.

K-023651.example: The stylesheet has no min-height rule, so the plan adds min-height: 2.75rem to the select. At a 16px root size that equals 44px.
K-023651.check: rg prints the new min-height line with a value of 2.75rem or 44px. The plan states the target is 44px at a 16px root font size.
traps: A small model may use 44 with no unit, which CSS ignores. Write 44px or 2.75rem.
Do not size only the visible label. The clickable area includes the whole select element.

steps.do: Count lines with physical left and right margin or padding properties in the src folder.
Count float declarations that use left or right values.
Count text-align values that are hard-coded to left or right.
List the files that contain margin-left or margin-right with line numbers.
Run stylelint on the stylesheets to record the baseline error count as a runner check.
Write the three totals into the plan and treat their sum as the number of declarations to convert, using the stylelint count as the baseline.

K-023652.example: rg -c prints src/main.css:14 and src/cards.css:6, so 20 margin and padding declarations need logical equivalents such as margin-inline-start. The float and text-align counts add to the total, so the plan lists them as separate work items. npx stylelint then prints its error count, which the plan records as the baseline.
K-023652.check: Each rg -c line prints file:count, the sum of the three totals is the number of declarations the plan must convert, and npx stylelint prints a numeric error count that the plan records; a file with no matches prints nothing.
traps: Small models count only one file and miss the rest of src.
Converting text-align: left to margin-inline-start by mistake; text-align needs start, not a margin.
Editing matches inside url() or content strings, which are not layout declarations.

steps.do: Count bytes in the English locale file as a rough length baseline.
Count bytes in the German locale file, which usually runs longer than English.
Count bytes in the Japanese locale file, which often runs shorter than English.
List all locale files to confirm the set of languages to budget for.
Run the label width test to confirm no label clips at 1.30 times the English width.
Set the label budget to 30 percent above the longest measured language and record the number in the plan.

K-023653.example: wc -c shows en.json at 4120 bytes and de.json at 5306 bytes, a ratio of 1.29. So the plan adds 30 percent slack and sets button min-width to 8rem (128px) with padding-inline set to 1rem. The playwright run then reports pass or fail for the label-width test at that budget.
K-023653.check: Each wc -c line prints a byte count, the longest ratio above 1.00 sets the slack, find prints one path per locale file, and npx playwright test prints a pass or fail count for label-width, where zero failures means the 1.30 budget holds.
traps: Byte counts are not character counts, so CJK text measures larger per character than Latin text.
Choosing a fixed width like 120px instead of min-width, which clips longer translations.
Using only English as the baseline, which hides expansion in German or French.

Check whether ar.json exists, which means Arabic pages must use dir rtl.
Check whether he.json exists, which means Hebrew pages must also use dir rtl.
Find where the html element is currently declared so the plan knows the base template.
Run the rtl test to confirm the html element reports dir rtl on the Arabic and Hebrew pages.
Write the mapping from each locale code to its lang and dir pair into the plan.

K-023654.check: test -f exits 0 when the file exists and 1 when it does not, rg -n prints the template line that holds the html tag, and npx playwright test prints a numeric failure count where 0 means the rtl test passed.
traps: Putting dir on body instead of html, so some browser UI and scrollbars stay left-to-right.
Setting dir on the whole page for mixed-language content, where dir=auto or a span with its own dir is correct.
Using a country code for lang instead of the locale code the file name uses.

steps.do: Count row-reverse and column-reverse declarations that would fight the automatic mirroring.
Count flex-direction declarations to see how many flex rows depend on direction.
Count grid-auto-flow declarations, since grid placement also follows the inline direction.
List direction-specific margin rules in the component files with line numbers.
Run the flex-order test to confirm the mirrored row matches the design order in rtl.
Record the plan: keep flex-direction row and let dir rtl mirror it, and remove each row-reverse rule unless the design requires a fixed order.

K-023655.example: rg -c shows row-reverse in src/nav.css at 2 matches, so the plan removes those rules because dir rtl already reverses the flex row. A row-reverse that stays is kept only where the design needs a fixed left-to-right order. The playwright run then prints a failure count for the rtl row order.
K-023655.check: rg -c prints file:count lines, after the plan the row-reverse count should be 0 unless the plan gives a reason for each remaining rule, and npx playwright test prints a numeric failure count where 0 means the mirrored order matches.
traps: Adding row-reverse under dir rtl, which mirrors the row twice and returns it to left-to-right order.
Assuming column layouts mirror; only the inline axis flips, so column-reverse is unaffected by dir.
Stopping at flex and forgetting that grid placement also depends on the writing direction.

Count :lang selectors already in the stylesheets, since per-language rules belong there.
Check for line-height declarations, which are the base that the per-script values override.

Writing :lang(ja) rules but never setting lang on the html element, so the selector never matches.
Setting the same line-height for CJK and Latin text, which leaves CJK lines cramped.

Confirm the toast container uses the fixed positioning classes.
